name: Client creative engagement (commission to accepted delivery)
one_line: Creative work made for an evidenced external or internal commissioning party, where a brief or scope opens a bounded job, review and approval connect revisions to that request, and a handoff or acceptance closes it. The same design files without a commissioner-maker relationship remain the creative default; the same relationship without a creative making record belongs to client/account, project-delivery, contract-administration, or consulting worlds. Placeholder J-IND row: it declares no fields and no serialized dimensions while the creative schema's project, stage, artifact_type, and client proposals await R1c.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: these are detection signals, not extraction licences. The creative schema declares no field rows, so this template writes no creative facts. Privacy policy is applied before any content reaches a model or connector.

a commissioned-BRIEF structure with explicit Client or Requester and Prepared by or Creative team roles, plus objective, audience, deliverables, schedule and approver blocks; the role pair and requested output together are stronger than either a creative brief shape or an organisation name

a signed PROPOSAL or statement of work that names the commissioning party and maker in distinct roles, describes creative deliverables, gives revision or approval mechanics, and is paired with at least one referenced working file, proof or delivery export

a REVIEW ROUND: same-project proofs or review links accompanied by comments from an identified client-side reviewer, followed by a revised same-stem asset; markup coordinates, time-coded comments or page annotations make the review relationship observable

a written APPROVAL or sign-off that identifies the exact proof, cut, layout or version accepted and crosses the commissioner-maker boundary; approval vocabulary without the identified artifact is insufficient
a DELIVERY MANIFEST or handoff note listing final creative assets, formats or variants and a recipient, paired with the named exported files; one export alone is not a delivery structure
an end-to-end packet or archive whose readable manifest contains a brief or scope, creative sources, review rounds, explicit approval, and final deliverables under one recurring job reference

a creative-request system export with labelled requester, creative owner, requested deliverables, workflow state and approval history, where the content shows a bounded request rather than a standing queue
needs_llm: deciding whether two organisation names describe commissioner and maker, the maker and a subcontractor, two brands depicted in the work, or merely sender and recipient; a model must cite the role-bearing text or return unknown

deciding whether an inbound commission enquiry became an accepted engagement; a request, budget suggestion or meeting invitation is not acceptance without a reply, scope, work product or other relationship evidence
distinguishing client feedback from internal art direction when an email says only 'please revise' and the sender role is not labelled
distinguishing a delivered client master from a portfolio copy, publication asset, DAM download or backup; the handoff context, not identical bytes, supplies the engagement evidence
deciding whether a purpose-coherent packet of brief, references, working sources, proofs, approval and exports is one commissioned job despite content and format diversity

separating an in-house creative request from a general internal project: an internal requester may be a client operationally, but the packet still needs a creative artifact moving through review to delivery

separating the creative work record from commercial and legal administration embedded in the same packet; one signed scope may be evidence for several schemas without transferring fees, obligations or legal effect into creative facts
never_alone: a client, brand, agency, studio or person name alone; the same entity may be commissioner, maker, employer, licensor, supplier, subject or cited competitor
the words client, commission, job, brief, scope, deliverable, feedback, approved or final alone; each also occurs in templates, internal work, legal instruments and generic project records
a creative source type or extension alone; file format routes extraction but does not establish a commissioner-maker relationship
a brief-shaped document alone: it may be blank, speculative, educational, downloaded, rejected or an enquiry that never became work
a contract or invoice alone: commercial administration does not prove a creative making record, and this row does not infer the service performed from an amount or parties block
a version token, FINAL suffix, Approved filename or signature image alone; approval needs the identified reviewer or sign-off context and the artifact it answers
an email thread, shared-drive folder, transfer link or bounded download session alone; transport and co-occurrence are not topic or engagement proof
a parent path named Clients, Jobs, Commissions or a brand name; existing vocabulary supports retrieval but cannot manufacture the role or relationship
an organisation gazetteer hit, author metadata, PDF company metadata or email signature alone
a bare date or four-digit number interpreted as deadline, job number, year or version
the absence of a fee, contract or external email as proof that work is self-initiated; in-house commissions and informal paid work may lack them

grouping_reasons: one commissioned job from accepted brief or scope through working sources, review, approval and delivery
one client relationship across several separately named creative projects, only after each project's own membership is evidenced
one review round: exact proof, client comments and the revision that answers them
one delivery set: manifest or handoff message and the exact format or market variants it lists
one change to scope and the additional creative work explicitly authorized by it
one request-system export and the assets or messages joined by exact request or job references
no group is valid for an isolated enquiry, blank brief, contract, invoice, brand asset or final-looking export

template.why: Empty by binding contract: the creative schema declares no field rows, so this template cannot serialize dimensions from its four pending proposals. Held as prose for R1c: when the schema proposals are adopted, client may come first only in a genuinely multi-client corpus, then project, then stage, then artifact_type; in a single-client or in-house corpus the client level must flatten because it would be a one-child collector. This row intentionally does not differ from the creative default in order. It survives the node test through narrower activation: a role-bearing brief, scope, review, approval or handoff connects a commissioner to the making record. Not time-first because dates of request, creation, review, approval and delivery are different clocks and a year-first tree would scatter one engagement.

collides_with.signal: The same client name, stakeholder emails, status deck and renewal conversation may appear in both. This row requires a bounded creative request plus a making artifact moving through review or delivery; customer-account-management owns standing relationship health, adoption, support and renewal evidence. Reciprocal fixture: Acme account quarterly review.pdf belongs there despite the word client; Northwind Final Artwork - delivery manifest.xlsx belongs here despite being sent to an account contact.

A creative engagement is also delivered as a project and may have the same charter, schedule, risks, status and acceptance page. This row requires commissioner-maker roles and a creative artifact lineage; project-delivery owns governance of a bounded effort where sponsor, dependencies, health and benefits are the anchor. Reciprocal fixture: Project Phoenix Weekly Status 2026-08-14.pptx stays there without creative work; a concept proof with client comments stays here without a governance apparatus.

A signed statement of work, change request and acceptance page are identical bytes on both sides. This row owns their membership in a creative making lifecycle; contract-administration owns the executed instrument, obligations, notices, renewal and commercial administration. Reciprocal fixture: Statement of Work - Northwind Rebrand - signed.pdf may carry both anchors, but an obligation register must not activate creative and a reviewed artwork must not activate contract administration.

Prepared-for and prepared-by roles, a scope, milestones, fees, feedback and acceptance occur in both. A linked or layered creative source, proof-to-revision lineage, or media delivery set supports this row; analytical recommendations, advisory work products and implementation plans without a creative making record support consulting. The same multidisciplinary engagement may contain members of both.

The creative sources and revision habits may be byte-for-byte identical. An evidenced commissioner-maker relationship and client-side review or acceptance supports this row; a self-set brief, personal release decision and absence of any accepted counterparty supports self-initiated work. Absence alone never proves the latter.

also_holds_with.signal: A signed creative-services agreement or rights instrument may be both legal evidence and a member of the commissioned making record. Legal owns parties, instrument and legal-status observations; this template owns only the evidenced relationship of that member to the creative workflow.

An invoice or paid receipt may independently carry Finance facts while an exact job reference supports membership in the engagement. Membership does not copy client or project facts and does not make payment a creative fact.
A screenshot of client markup or photographed physical proof retains positive capture evidence while OCR and exact review references support engagement membership. Missing EXIF proves neither side.

A delivered client work may later be selected as the maker's portfolio sample. The commissioned production record and the authored career evidence coexist; portfolio selection is not inferred from delivery.

falls_through_to.why: A durable standalone brief, approval, handoff note or readable agreement with no accepted engagement group remains an independent record rather than forcing a client branch.
An enquiry, unlabelled feedback email, final-looking export or mixed kickoff archive whose roles and relationship are unresolved needs review rather than invented engagement facts.
Blank creative brief templates, downloaded example scopes and inspirational client-work case studies are references when no live job evidence exists.
An isolated invoice, transfer confirmation or service receipt retains its financial purpose when the creative engagement does not fire.
An unreadable transfer package or password-protected client archive is represented safely without manufacturing a relationship from its filename.
A readable but isolated agreement, NDA, unreleased launch brief or contact-bearing approval may require local protection even when no engagement group is accepted.

role_split.why: The proposed client key is the commissioning counterparty, never the maker's own studio or employer. A Prepared for / Prepared by pair is useful only if the two roles remain distinct; the creative schema's proposal records the canonical client/our_firm split, while this template adds no field rows.

sensitivity_why: Briefs and reviews often expose unreleased products, campaigns, prices, strategy, named contacts, personal likenesses, client-supplied assets, credentials or transfer links; contracts and invoices add commercial and personal data. Recognition should use local structure and minimal excerpts, suppress raw previews in broad summaries, and never infer that publication or delivery made the surrounding engagement public. This is a catalogue posture, not a handling class or legal conclusion.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: (1) confirm that a distinct client-engagement template survives despite sharing the creative default's future dimension order; this row argues that role-bearing brief/review/approval/delivery activation is materially narrower. (2) Decide whether in-house requester work may use canonical client or needs a separate requester role; minting a synonym here would pre-empt R1c. (3) Decide whether client may be a visible first dimension at all, and require flattening for single-client and in-house corpora. (4) Set the reciprocal rule with customer-account-management: a bounded creative job may group by client after approval, while a standing account queue must not acquire that branch. (5) Specify how exact review, approval and delivery membership is recorded without copying client, project or stage facts onto sparse members.
